Definition: from ἀγείρω (to gather; probably akin to G1453); properly, the town-square (as a place of public resort); by implication, a market or thoroughfare:--market(-place), street.
BiblicalUsage: Agora is the marketplace — the town square, the public place where life happened. Jesus compares His generation to children sitting in the markets; the householder finds labourers standing idle in the marketplace; the sick are laid in the marketplaces hoping to touch Jesus' garment; and Paul disputed daily in the market at Athens with those who met him.
TheologicalSignificance: Children calling in the marketplace is the Lord's picture of a generation that would not dance — the place is the stage, not the lesson.
